- **Memory Complexity**: $O(N_{solid} \cdot C + N_{runs})$, where $N_{solid}$ is the number of solid voxels, $C$ is color bits, and $N_{runs}$ is the number of RLE entries.

RLE4 Compression converts a dense 3D voxel grid into a sparse, column-oriented structure called **Map4** to solve memory bloat in large volumes with significant empty space [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the compression algorithm converts a 3D voxel grid into a sparse Run-Length Encoded (RLE) structure called Map4. It further confirms that this structure is column-oriented (processing XZ planes and encoding along the Y-axis) and that the purpose is to solve memory bloat in large volumes by compressing contiguous air/solid regions.

It processes the volume slice-by-slice (XZ planes), encoding runs of empty space (skip) and occupied space (solid) along the Y-axis into 16-bit words, while storing per-voxel color and intensity data in a separate texture buffer [S1, unofficial].
